Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] MFA fatigue spam: ≥5 failed prompts followed by success approval from new device · [LLM] Help-desk-style password/MFA reset immediately followed by successful sign-in from new geo
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Privileged role assignment within 15 minutes of first-ever interactive sign-in by user · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rogue VM / virtual-disk provisioning followed by cross-tenant disk mount · [LLM] New service principal / app registration granted broad consent within 1h of admin sign-in · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Sustained large-volume egress from VPN/RDP gateway host to cloud storage in <72min · [LLM] Pre-impact log clearing (wevtutil) and shadow-copy destruction within 72-min win · [LLM] Cross-host lateral movement fan-out from a single newly-authed account within 60min · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
MFA fatigue spam: ≥5 failed prompts followed by success approval from new device AIDelivery High
Detects the Muddled Libra/Scattered Spider initial-access pattern where the actor floods a user with MFA push prompts until they approve. Correlates a burst of MFA failures (ErrorCode 50140/500121) against the same UPN with a subsequent successful interactive sign-in from a previously unseen device/IP. Rationale: Article: 'Initial access is often gained through compromised credentials, MFA manipulation' and Unit 42 IR Report cites 65% identity-driven access. Codes 50140/500121/50158 are documented MFA-prompt fail codes used by Scattered Spider per Microsoft Threat Intel. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2023/09/14/octo-tempest/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1015/
ATT&CKT1621 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User loses phone, repeatedly fails Authenticator then succeeds after recovery
  • Slow/poor connectivity causing MFA prompt timeouts before eventual success
  • Conditional Access policy churn during a migration window
  • New corporate laptop registration after IT-issued password reset
  • User travelling, hitting Authenticator from a foreign IP after airport Wi-Fi failures
Suppression filter
and IPAddress !in (dynamic(["<corporate egress IPs>"])) and Country !in ((IdentityInfo | where AccountUpn == AccountUpn | summarize make_set(Country))[0])
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the AccountUpn's SigninLogs for the prior 24h, confirm the approving device/IP is not in IdentityInfo's known device list; check IdentityInfo.AssignedRoles for privileged status. 2) Contain: revoke all refresh tokens (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken / Revoke-MgUserSignInSession), require password reset + re-register MFA, raise sign-in risk to High to force CA block. 3) Hunt: pivot on AccountObjectId across AuditLogs for role/group changes in the next 60min; CloudAppEvents for OAuth consents; DeviceLogonEvents for any RemoteInteractive sessions sourced from the same IP/ASN.
let Window = 10m;
let Failures = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ErrorCode in (50140, 500121, 50158)
| summarize FailureCount = count(), FailureIPs = make_set(IPAddress,5), FirstFail = min(Timestamp), LastFail = max(Timestamp) by AccountUpn, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| where FailureCount >= 5;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ErrorCode == 0 and IsInteractive == true
| join kind=inner Failures on AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (LastFail .. LastFail + 5m)
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, DeviceName, Application, FailureCount, FailureIPs, FirstFail, LastFail
let Window = 10m;
let Failures = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType in (50140, 500121, 50158)
| summarize FailureCount = count(), FailureIPs = make_set(IPAddress,5), FirstFail = min(TimeGenerated), LastFail = max(TimeGenerated) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| where FailureCount >= 5;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType == 0 and IsInteractive == true
| join kind=inner Failures on UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (LastFail .. LastFail + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, FailureCount, FailureIPs, FirstFail, LastFail
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:(50140 OR 500121 OR 50158)
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog EventResult=Failure | groupBy([UserPrincipalName], function=[count(as=Failures), max(_time, as=LastFail)]) | Failures>=5
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.signature_id IN ("50140","500121","50158") by Authentication.user _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where count >= 5 | join type=inner user [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as success_time from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where success_time > _time AND success_time < _time + 600
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.signature_id IN ("50140","500121","50158") by Authentication.user _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where count >= 5 | join type=inner user [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as success_time from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where success_time > _time AND success_time < _time + 600
Help-desk-style password/MFA reset immediately followed by successful sign-in from new geo AIDelivery High
Hunts the Scattered Spider help-desk impersonation pattern: admin or help-desk role resets a user's password or MFA method, and within 30 minutes that user signs in from an IP/country not previously seen for them. Specifically targets the social-entry vector called out in the article. Rationale: Article explicitly cites 'help-desk impersonation' as a primary initial-access tactic. Mandiant + MSRC OctoTempest write-ups confirm Scattered Spider social-engineers help-desk staff to reset MFA/passwords then sign in within minutes from actor infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/unc3944-targeted-attacks • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2023/10/25/octo-tempest-crosses-boundaries/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1556.006
Data sourcesChange Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate help-desk ticket: user lost phone, IT resets MFA, user re-registers from home (new IP)
  • Onboarding/offboarding admin provisioning new starter accounts
  • Self-service password reset where SSPR audit log lists 'Self-service' as initiator
  • Travelling executive calling support from a hotel, then signing in immediately after reset
  • Tenant-wide MFA rollout where a script resets methods in bulk
Suppression filter
and Initiator !in (dynamic(["<help-desk svc accounts>","<SSPR system>"])) and DeviceDetail !contains "Compliant"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm Initiator's identity against an authoritative ticketing record; check whether the target user has Global/Privileged Admin roles via IdentityInfo.AssignedRoles. 2) Contain: revoke target's sessions, suspend the account, contact the user out-of-band before re-enabling; if Initiator account is also suspicious, force their reset too. 3) Hunt: enumerate all reset operations Initiator performed in last 24h, plus all sign-ins from the new IP/ASN across the tenant; check CloudAppEvents for OAuth grants made by the target post-reset.
let Resets = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName in ("Reset user password","Update user","Update authentication methods of user","Admin registered security info","Admin updated security info","User registered security info")
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName), Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(TargetUpn) and TargetUpn != Initiator
| project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, TargetUpn, Initiator, OperationName;
Resets
| join kind=inner (SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where ResultType == 0
    | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, DeviceDetail
  ) on $left.TargetUpn == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (ResetTime .. ResetTime + 30m)
| join kind=leftouter (IdentityInfo | summarize KnownCountries = make_set(Country) by AccountUpn) on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.AccountUpn
| extend NewGeo = iff(Location !in (KnownCountries), true, false)
| where NewGeo == true
| project ResetTime, Initiator, UserPrincipalName, SigninTime = TimeGenerated, Location, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, DeviceDetail
let Resets = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName in ("Reset user password","Update user","Update authentication methods of user","Admin registered security info","Admin updated security info","User registered security info")
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName), Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(TargetUpn) and TargetUpn != Initiator
| project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, TargetUpn, Initiator, OperationName;
Resets
| join kind=inner (SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where ResultType == 0
    | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, DeviceDetail) on $left.TargetUpn == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (ResetTime .. ResetTime + 30m)
| join kind=leftouter (IdentityInfo | summarize KnownCountries = make_set(Country) by AccountUpn) on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Location !in (KnownCountries)
| project ResetTime, Initiator, UserPrincipalName, SigninTime = TimeGenerated, Location, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, DeviceDetail
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Reset user password" OR "Update authentication methods of user" OR "Admin registered security info")

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as reset_time from datamodel=Change where Change.action=modified Change.object_category=user Change.change_type IN ("password reset","mfa registered","strongAuthenticationPhoneAppDetail") by Change.src_user Change.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as target_user | join type=inner target_user [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as login_time values(Authentication.src) as src_ip from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as target_user] | where login_time > reset_time AND login_time < reset_time + 1800
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as reset_time from datamodel=Change where Change.action=modified Change.object_category=user Change.change_type IN ("password reset","mfa registered","strongAuthenticationPhoneAppDetail") by Change.src_user Change.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as target_user | join type=inner target_user [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as login_time values(Authentication.src) as src_ip from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as target_user] | where login_time > reset_time AND login_time < reset_time + 1800
Privileged role assignment within 15 minutes of first-ever interactive sign-in by user AIExploitation High
Detects the Spoiled Scorpius/Muddled Libra escalation pattern of going from valid-user to Global Admin within minutes. Correlates AuditLogs role-assignment events with the actor's first successful interactive sign-in for that user, surfacing rapid privilege escalation that bypasses normal change-management cadence. Rationale: Article: 'attackers frequently attempt privilege escalation and administrative account abuse within minutes or hours.' Time-bounded join surfaces the operationally improbable 'new admin signs in then grants Global Admin in 15 min' shape unique to compromise vs. legitimate change. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/003/ • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/unc3944-sms-phishing-uses-legitimate-tools
ATT&CKT1098.003 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Break-glass account first-use during a real DR drill
  • New CISO/IT admin onboarding day-one provisioning
  • PIM activation of an already-eligible role (filter on activation events)
  • M&A-related bulk role grants by a PMO admin
  • Identity Governance access-package fulfillment driven by HR-onboarding workflow
Suppression filter
and Initiator !in (dynamic(["<break-glass UPNs>"])) and not (OperationName has "PIM")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull Initiator's IdentityInfo and SigninLogs for past 30 days — was this their first-ever interactive sign-in this tenant? Compare IP/UA against IdentityInfo. 2) Contain: remove the role assignment, revoke target's sessions, suspend Initiator account, disable any new credentials added in the window. 3) Hunt: enumerate every AuditLogs operation by Initiator and TargetUpn for next 4h; check AzureActivity for new VM/storage/service-principal creation; CloudAppEvents for OAuth consent grants by the elevated account.
let RoleOps = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName in ("Add member to role","Add eligible member to role","Add member to role completed (PIM activation)","Add app role assignment to service principal","Add member to group")
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName), Role = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources.modifiedProperties))[1].newValue), Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| where Role has_any ("Global Administrator","Privileged Role Administrator","User Administrator","Application Administrator","Cloud Application Administrator","Helpdesk Administrator","Privileged Authentication Administrator")
| project RoleTime = TimeGenerated, Initiator, TargetUpn, Role;
RoleOps
| join kind=inner (SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where ResultType == 0 and IsInteractive == true
    | summarize FirstLogin = min(TimeGenerated), IPAddress = any(IPAddress), Location = any(Location) by UserPrincipalName) on $left.Initiator == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where RoleTime between (FirstLogin .. FirstLogin + 15m)
| project FirstLogin, RoleTime, MinutesAfterLogon = datetime_diff('minute', RoleTime, FirstLogin), Initiator, TargetUpn, Role, IPAddress, Location
let RoleOps = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName in ("Add member to role","Add eligible member to role","Add app role assignment to service principal")
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName), Role = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources.modifiedProperties))[1].newValue), Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| where Role has_any ("Global Administrator","Privileged Role Administrator","User Administrator","Application Administrator","Cloud Application Administrator","Privileged Authentication Administrator")
| project RoleTime = TimeGenerated, Initiator, TargetUpn, Role;
RoleOps
| join kind=inner (SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where ResultType == 0 and IsInteractive == true
    | summarize FirstLogin = min(TimeGenerated), IPAddress = any(IPAddress), Location = any(Location) by UserPrincipalName) on $left.Initiator == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where RoleTime between (FirstLogin .. FirstLogin + 15m)
| join kind=leftouter (IdentityInfo | summarize PriorRoles = make_set(AssignedRoles) by AccountUpn) on $left.Initiator == $right.AccountUpn
| where PriorRoles !has "Global Administrator"
| project FirstLogin, RoleTime, MinutesAfterLogon = datetime_diff('minute', RoleTime, FirstLogin), Initiator, TargetUpn, Role, IPAddress, Location
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Add member to role" OR "Add eligible member to role")
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as role_time values(Change.object) as role_assigned from datamodel=Change where Change.change_type="role assignment" by Change.user Change.src_user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as actor | join type=inner actor [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as first_login from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as actor] | where role_time < first_login + 900
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as role_time values(Change.object) as role_assigned from datamodel=Change where Change.change_type="role assignment" by Change.user Change.src_user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as actor | join type=inner actor [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as first_login from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as actor] | where role_time < first_login + 900
Rogue VM / virtual-disk provisioning followed by cross-tenant disk mount AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the article's 'create rogue virtual machines, mount virtual drives' tradecraft. Pivots AzureActivity write operations on VMs/disks where the caller has no prior provisioning history in that region or subscription within the past 30 days. Rationale: Article: 'they may provision cloud resources, create rogue virtual machines, mount virtual drives or establish persistence to support data staging and exfiltration.' The leftanti baseline on Caller+Region surfaces the unfamiliar-actor signal without alerting on routine deployments. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1578/002/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/muddled-libra/
ATT&CKT1578.002 T1578.004
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform/Bicep CI runner first deploy in a new region
  • DR test creating standby VMs in a secondary region
  • Newly onboarded DevOps engineer's first provision
  • Auto-scaler creating compute in an off-hours window
  • Disk snapshot taken as part of a Veeam/Azure Backup job
Suppression filter
and Caller !endswith "@<corp-deploy-svc-domain>" and CallerIpAddress !in (dynamic(["<known-CI-egress-IPs>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify Caller's identity (UPN, ServicePrincipal, ManagedIdentity), correlate AuditLogs for any recent role changes for that principal, inspect the deployed VM's NIC for public IP exposure. 2) Contain: stop the VM, deny inbound NSG rules, revoke caller's tokens, disable the ServicePrincipal if it's the actor. 3) Hunt: pivot Caller across all AzureActivity in last 24h, look for disk-attach across subscriptions, OfficeActivity for new SharePoint/OneDrive share-links, AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs for SP IP origin.
let Baseline = AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
| where OperationNameValue has_any ("Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write","Microsoft.Compute/disks/write","Microsoft.Compute/disks/beginGetAccess/action")
| summarize KnownCallers = make_set(Caller), KnownRegions = make_set(tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).resourceLocation)) by SubscriptionId;
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ActivityStatusValue in ("Success","Succeeded","Start")
| where OperationNameValue has_any ("Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write","Microsoft.Compute/disks/write","Microsoft.Compute/disks/beginGetAccess/action","Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/write","Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/attachDataDisk/action")
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on SubscriptionId
| extend Region = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).resourceLocation)
| where Caller !in (KnownCallers) or Region !in (KnownRegions)
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, OperationNameValue, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup, ResourceId, Region, KnownCallers, KnownRegions
source:azure.activity_logs @operationName.value:(Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write OR Microsoft.Compute/disks/write OR Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/write OR Microsoft.Compute/disks/beginGetAccess/action)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, awsRegion, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters.instanceType, requestParameters.snapshotId
| filter eventName in ["RunInstances", "CreateVolume", "CreateSnapshot", "AttachVolume", "CopySnapshot", "ModifySnapshotAttribute"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and userIdentity.type in ["IAMUser", "AssumedRole", "Federated", "SAMLUser"]
| sort @timestamp desc

New service principal / app registration granted broad consent within 1h of admin sign-in AIInstallation Medium
Targets the Scattered Spider persistence trick of standing up a fresh app/service-principal with broad delegated/application permissions immediately after escalation, so that loss of the user account doesn't break C2/data access. Rationale: Article: '...establish persistence to support data staging and exfiltration.' Service-principal abuse is the Scattered Spider/Spoiled Scorpius persistence of choice — survives password resets. Risky-scope list mirrors MSRC's documented OAuth-abuse permissions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/01/25/midnight-blizzard-guidance-for-responders-on-nation-state-attack/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/001/
ATT&CKT1098.001 T1136.003
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC team registering a new SIEM connector / Graph reader app
  • M365 third-party-app integration during a planned procurement
  • Power Platform/Logic Apps creating SP for managed connector
  • ISV deploying a new add-in following admin consent flow
  • Custom internal tooling rotating to a fresh SP for least-privilege
Suppression filter
and AppName !in (dynamic(["<approved 1P app names>"])) and Initiator !endswith "@<your-deployment-svc-domain>"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the AppName/AppId, check Microsoft's public app catalog and tenant publisher verification, review the consent scope against IT's app-onboarding tickets. 2) Contain: disable the SP (Set-AzureADServicePrincipal -AccountEnabled false), revoke OAuth grants (Remove-AzureADOAuth2PermissionGrant), block sign-in for the app. 3) Hunt: AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs for IPs the SP authenticated from, CloudAppEvents for any Graph/Exchange/SharePoint reads under the SP, AzureActivity for resource provisioning by the SP.
let Risky = dynamic(["Mail.ReadWrite.All","Mail.Send","Mail.Send.All","Files.ReadWrite.All","Sites.FullControl.All","Directory.ReadWrite.All","Application.ReadWrite.All","AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All","RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory","User.ReadWrite.All"]);
let AppCreate = CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Add application.","Add service principal.","Add owner to application.","Add owner to service principal.")
| extend Initiator = AccountDisplayName, AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).Target[3].ID)
| project AppCreateTime = Timestamp, Initiator, AppName;
AppCreate
| join kind=inner (CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add app role assignment grant to user.","Add delegated permission grant.")
    | extend ConsentScope = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ModifiedProperties)
    | where ConsentScope has_any (Risky)
    | project ConsentTime = Timestamp, ConsentInitiator = AccountDisplayName, ConsentScope, AppId = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ObjectId)) on $left.Initiator == $right.ConsentInitiator
| where ConsentTime between (AppCreateTime .. AppCreateTime + 1h)
| project AppCreateTime, ConsentTime, Initiator, AppName, ConsentScope
let Risky = dynamic(["Mail.ReadWrite.All","Mail.Send","Files.ReadWrite.All","Sites.FullControl.All","Directory.ReadWrite.All","Application.ReadWrite.All","AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All","RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory","User.ReadWrite.All"]);
let AppCreate = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in ("Add application","Add service principal","Add owner to application","Add owner to service principal")
| extend Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend AppName = tostring(TargetResources.displayName)
| project AppCreateTime = TimeGenerated, Initiator, AppName;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add app role assignment grant to user","Add delegated permission grant","Add app role assignment to service principal")
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend ConsentScope = tostring(TargetResources.modifiedProperties), Initiator2 = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| where ConsentScope has_any (Risky)
| join kind=inner AppCreate on $left.Initiator2 == $right.Initiator
| where TimeGenerated between (AppCreateTime .. AppCreateTime + 1h)
| project AppCreateTime, ConsentTime = TimeGenerated, Initiator = Initiator2, AppName, ConsentScope
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Add application" OR "Add service principal" OR "Consent to application" OR "Add delegated permission grant")
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as create_time values(Change.object) as app_name from datamodel=Change where Change.change_type IN ("application created","service principal created") by Change.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as Initiator | join type=left Initiator [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as consent_time values(Change.object) as scope from datamodel=Change where Change.change_type="oauth consent" by Change.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as Initiator] | where consent_time > create_time AND consent_time < create_time + 3600
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as create_time values(Change.object) as app_name from datamodel=Change where Change.change_type IN ("application created","service principal created") by Change.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as Initiator | join type=left Initiator [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as consent_time values(Change.object) as scope from datamodel=Change where Change.change_type="oauth consent" by Change.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as Initiator] | where consent_time > create_time AND consent_time < create_time + 3600
Sustained large-volume egress from VPN/RDP gateway host to cloud storage in <72min AIActions on Objectives Medium
Targets the Spoiled Scorpius pattern of exfiltrating hundreds of GB within hours via the same remote-access infrastructure used for entry. Aggregates outbound bytes from internal hosts to known cloud-storage destinations, flagging hosts whose 1h volume vs. the host's 7-day baseline jumps >10x. Rationale: Article quotes Spoiled Scorpius 'exfiltrated hundreds of gigabytes of data within hours of gaining access through improperly secured remote access infrastructure.' 5GB/1h with 10x baseline jump is the documented signal Unit 42 used in the RansomHub IR. Cloud-storage domain list per Unit42 RansomHub blog + abuse.ch. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/threat-assessment-howling-scorpius-akira-ransomware/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineer pushing a fresh container image to S3/Blob/GCS
  • Backup software (Veeam Cloud Connect, MSP backup) staging to cloud
  • Video-conf recording upload after an all-hands
  • Mass photo/document upload by Marketing to a cloud asset library
  • Application telemetry shipping crash dumps after a release
Suppression filter
and SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<backup server IPs>","<CI build agents>"])) and SourceUserName !in (dynamic(["<backup svc accounts>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user/process behind the traffic; check if the host is a known backup target via MachineGroup; review InitiatingProcessFileName — legitimate (e.g. aws.exe, azcopy.exe) vs. living-off-the-land. 2) Contain: block the destination domain at proxy/firewall, isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill long-running upload processes. 3) Hunt: pivot SourceUserName across AADSignInEventsBeta for fresh anomalous auth, DeviceFileEvents for staging directories (Temp, ProgramData), OfficeActivity for SharePoint/OneDrive bulk-download events that fed the staging.
let CloudStorage = dynamic(["s3.amazonaws.com","blob.core.windows.net","storage.googleapis.com","mega.nz","transfer.sh","anonfiles.com","file.io","pcloud.com","backblazeb2.com","wasabisys.com","dropboxapi.com","box.com"]);
let Baseline = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp between (ago(7d) .. ago(2h))
| where RemoteUrl has_any (CloudStorage)
| summarize BaselineHourlyBytes = avg(toreal(tostring(parse_json(tostring(AdditionalFields)).bytes_out))) by DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(2h)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (CloudStorage)
| extend BytesOut = toreal(tostring(parse_json(tostring(AdditionalFields)).bytes_out))
| summarize TotalBytes = sum(BytesOut), DistinctRemotes = dcount(RemoteUrl), Procs = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName,8), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on DeviceName
| where TotalBytes > 5368709120 and (isnull(BaselineHourlyBytes) or TotalBytes > BaselineHourlyBytes * 10)
| project DeviceName, FirstSeen, LastSeen, TotalBytesGB = TotalBytes/1073741824.0, BaselineGB = BaselineHourlyBytes/1073741824.0, DistinctRemotes, Procs
let CloudStorage = dynamic(["s3.amazonaws.com","blob.core.windows.net","storage.googleapis.com","mega.nz","transfer.sh","anonfiles.com","file.io","pcloud.com","backblazeb2.com","wasabisys.com"]);
let Baseline = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(7d) .. ago(2h))
| where DestinationHostName has_any (CloudStorage) or RequestURL has_any (CloudStorage)
| summarize BaselineHourlyBytes = avg(toreal(SentBytes)) by SourceIP;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (CloudStorage) or RequestURL has_any (CloudStorage)
| summarize TotalBytes = sum(toreal(SentBytes)), Hosts = dcount(DestinationHostName), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SourceIP, SourceUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on SourceIP
| where TotalBytes > 5368709120 and (isnull(BaselineHourlyBytes) or TotalBytes > BaselineHourlyBytes * 10)
| project SourceIP, SourceUserName, FirstSeen, LastSeen, TotalBytesGB = TotalBytes/1073741824.0, BaselineGB = BaselineHourlyBytes/1073741824.0, Hosts
@network.bytes_written:>5368709120 @network.destination.hostname:(*.s3.amazonaws.com OR *.blob.core.windows.net OR *.storage.googleapis.com OR mega.nz OR transfer.sh OR anonfiles.com)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 | regex("(amazonaws|blob\.core|googleapis|mega\.nz|transfer\.sh|anonfiles)", field=ContextImageFileName) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[sum(SentBytes, as=TotalBytes), count(as=Conns)]) | TotalBytes>5368709120
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcaddr, dstaddr, dstport, bytes, action
| filter action = "ACCEPT" and bytes > 100000000
| stats sum(bytes) as totalBytes, count(*) as flows by srcaddr, bin(1h)
| filter totalBytes > 5368709120
| sort totalBytes desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(All_Traffic.dest) as dests from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_category="cloud_storage" OR All_Traffic.dest IN ("*.s3.amazonaws.com","*.blob.core.windows.net","*.storage.googleapis.com","mega.nz","transfer.sh","anonfiles.com","file.io") by All_Traffic.src _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | join type=left src [| tstats `summariesonly` avg(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as baseline from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_category="cloud_storage" earliest=-7d@d latest=-1d@d by All_Traffic.src _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | stats avg(baseline) as baseline by src] | where bytes_out > 5368709120 AND (isnull(baseline) OR bytes_out > baseline * 10)
| tstats summariesonly=false sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(All_Traffic.dest) as dests from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_category="cloud_storage" OR All_Traffic.dest IN ("*.s3.amazonaws.com","*.blob.core.windows.net","*.storage.googleapis.com","mega.nz","transfer.sh","anonfiles.com","file.io") by All_Traffic.src _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | join type=left src [| tstats summariesonly=false avg(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as baseline from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_category="cloud_storage" earliest=-7d@d latest=-1d@d by All_Traffic.src _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | stats avg(baseline) as baseline by src] | where bytes_out > 5368709120 AND (isnull(baseline) OR bytes_out > baseline * 10)
Pre-impact log clearing (wevtutil) and shadow-copy destruction within 72-min win AIActions on Objectives High
RansomHub/Spoiled Scorpius pre-encryption ritual: clear Windows event logs, delete VSS shadow copies, wipe the backup catalog, and disable Windows recovery — all within a tight time window. Surfaces the compound chain of all four destructive ops on the same host within an hour. Rationale: Article: 'distributors of RansomHub ransomware' — RansomHub's leaked playbook (per Symantec, BleepingComputer) walks wevtutil + vssadmin + wbadmin + bcdedit in sequence before encryption. Requiring ≥2 distinct destructive op-kinds on the same host within 1h is the chain signature. Replaces previous attempt that incorrectly referenced columns that don't exist on DeviceProcessEvents — now uses canonical ProcessCommandLine pattern matching only. Cross-checked against: • https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/ransomhub-knight-ransomware • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
ATT&CKT1070.001 T1490
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Veeam/Commvault backup job calling vssadmin pre-snapshot cleanup
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting VSS-corruption running vssadmin delete shadows manually
  • Windows imaging task using bcdedit during deployment
  • DC promotion script clearing event logs as part of build
  • DISM/SCCM maintenance task hitting wbadmin for catalog rebuild
Suppression filter
and Parents !has "VeeamBackup" and AccountName !in (dynamic(["<backup-svc>","<imaging-svc>"])) and not (Parents has "services.exe" and OpsSeen has_cs "ShadowDelete" and DistinctOpKinds == 2 and OpsSeen !has "LogClear")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm initiating account isn't a backup/imaging service account; pull AccountName's other DeviceProcessEvents in last 1h for ransomware-binary execution or mass file rename; check DeviceFileEvents for .ransom/.locked extensions appearing on the host. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, kill any active ransomware process (look for sustained DeviceFileEvents writes), snapshot for forensics, block lateral SMB from the host. 3) Hunt: pivot AccountName across DeviceLogonEvents for RDP/WinRM lateral hops in last 4h; DeviceNetworkEvents for known RansomHub C2 ASNs; AADSignInEventsBeta if the account is cloud-joined to find the original compromise.
let Window = 1h;
let Destructive = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend OpKind = case(
    FileName =~ "wevtutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any (" cl "," clear-log","/e:false"), "LogClear",
    FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete shadows", "ShadowDelete",
    FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadowcopy","delete"), "ShadowDelete",
    FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy","Remove-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy","Get-CimInstance Win32_Shadowcopy"), "ShadowDelete",
    FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("delete catalog","delete systemstatebackup","delete backup"), "BackupCatalogDelete",
    FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("recoveryenabled","no") or ProcessCommandLine has_all ("bootstatuspolicy","ignoreallfailures")), "RecoveryDisable",
    "")
| where isnotempty(OpKind)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, OpKind, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
Destructive
| summarize DistinctOpKinds = dcount(OpKind), OpsSeen = make_set(OpKind), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Samples = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10), Parents = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| where DistinctOpKinds >= 2
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, WindowMinutes, DeviceName, AccountName, DistinctOpKinds, OpsSeen, Parents, Samples
let Window = 1h;
let Destructive = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend NewProcessNameLower = tolower(NewProcessName), CmdLower = tolower(CommandLine)
| extend OpKind = case(
    NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\wevtutil.exe" and (CmdLower has " cl " or CmdLower has " clear-log" or CmdLower has "/e:false"), "LogClear",
    NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\vssadmin.exe" and CmdLower has "delete shadows", "ShadowDelete",
    NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\wmic.exe" and CmdLower has "shadowcopy" and CmdLower has "delete", "ShadowDelete",
    (NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (CmdLower has "win32_shadowcopy" or CmdLower has "remove-wmiobject win32_shadowcopy"), "ShadowDelete",
    NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\wbadmin.exe" and (CmdLower has "delete catalog" or CmdLower has "delete systemstatebackup" or CmdLower has "delete backup"), "BackupCatalogDelete",
    NewProcessNameLower endswith "\\bcdedit.exe" and ((CmdLower has "recoveryenabled" and CmdLower has " no") or (CmdLower has "bootstatuspolicy" and CmdLower has "ignoreallfailures")), "RecoveryDisable",
    "")
| where isnotempty(OpKind)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName, OpKind, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName;
Destructive
| summarize DistinctOpKinds = dcount(OpKind), OpsSeen = make_set(OpKind), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Samples = make_set(CommandLine, 10), Parents = make_set(ParentProcessName, 5) by Computer, AccountName, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| where DistinctOpKinds >= 2
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, WindowMinutes, Computer, AccountName, DistinctOpKinds, OpsSeen, Parents, Samples
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\\wevtutil.exe OR *\\WEVTUTIL.EXE OR *\\vssadmin.exe OR *\\VSSADMIN.EXE OR *\\wbadmin.exe OR *\\WBADMIN.EXE OR *\\bcdedit.exe OR *\\BCDEDIT.EXE) @CommandLine:(*"delete shadows"* OR *"delete catalog"* OR *"clear-log"* OR *" cl "* OR *"recoveryenabled no"* OR *"ignoreallfailures"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | ImageFileName=/\\(wevtutil|vssadmin|wmic|wbadmin|bcdedit)\.exe$/i | regex("(delete\s+shadows|delete\s+catalog|clear-log|\scl\s|recoveryenabled\s+no|ignoreallfailures|shadowcopy.*delete)", field=CommandLine, flags="i") | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=[count(field=ImageFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctTools), collect([CommandLine])]) | DistinctTools>=2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmd_samples from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="wevtutil.exe" Processes.process IN ("*cl *","* cl *","*clear-log*")) OR (Processes.process_name="vssadmin.exe" Processes.process="*delete shadows*") OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" Processes.process="*shadowcopy*delete*") OR (Processes.process_name="wbadmin.exe" Processes.process IN ("*delete catalog*","*delete systemstatebackup*","*delete backup*")) OR (Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe" Processes.process IN ("*recoveryenabled*no*","*bootstatuspolicy*ignoreallfailures*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | stats dc(eval(case(match(cmd_samples,"wevtutil"),"log", match(cmd_samples,"vssadmin|shadowcopy"),"shadow", match(cmd_samples,"wbadmin"),"backup", match(cmd_samples,"bcdedit"),"recovery"))) as DestructiveOpKinds values(cmd_samples) as cmd_samples by dest user _time | where DestructiveOpKinds >= 2
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmd_samples from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="wevtutil.exe" Processes.process IN ("*cl *","* cl *","*clear-log*")) OR (Processes.process_name="vssadmin.exe" Processes.process="*delete shadows*") OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" Processes.process="*shadowcopy*delete*") OR (Processes.process_name="wbadmin.exe" Processes.process IN ("*delete catalog*","*delete systemstatebackup*","*delete backup*")) OR (Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe" Processes.process IN ("*recoveryenabled*no*","*bootstatuspolicy*ignoreallfailures*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | stats dc(eval(case(match(cmd_samples,"wevtutil"),"log", match(cmd_samples,"vssadmin|shadowcopy"),"shadow", match(cmd_samples,"wbadmin"),"backup", match(cmd_samples,"bcdedit"),"recovery"))) as DestructiveOpKinds values(cmd_samples) as cmd_samples by dest user _time | where DestructiveOpKinds >= 2
Cross-host lateral movement fan-out from a single newly-authed account within 60min AIActions on Objectives Medium
Targets the article's 'multi-surface pivot' — same identity authenticating into ≥3 internal hosts (RDP/WinRM/SMB) within an hour of first interactive logon, the Muddled Libra hands-on-keyboard signature. Rationale: Article: 'attackers increasingly move across identity, endpoint, cloud and SaaS environments.' 3-host fan-out within 1h with no prior baseline is the classic Scattered Spider hands-on-keyboard pattern Unit 42 has surfaced in IR engagements. Anti-join against 30d baseline kills the 'admin who logs into 20 hosts daily' FP class. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/unc3944-targeted-attacks • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1021.006 T1550.002
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • New domain admin's first day onboarding and touring infrastructure
  • SCCM/Intune enrollment day where an installer account hits many hosts
  • Vulnerability-scanner credentialed scan that wasn't allowlisted
  • BloodHound/AzureHound assessment by a red team or consultant
  • Audit/compliance script enumerating Windows hosts for inventory
Suppression filter
and AccountName !in (dynamic(["<scanner svc>","<sccm push svc>","<vuln-scan svc>"])) and Sources !has "<scanner subnet>"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull AccountName's IdentityInfo + recent SigninLogs — was the cloud sign-in flagged as Risky? Are the host pivot destinations grouped (one OU) or spread (suspicious)? 2) Contain: disable the AD account, force Kerberos ticket purge across domain, isolate the originating source IP host. 3) Hunt: pivot the sources IP across DeviceNetworkEvents for inbound RDP/WinRM, DeviceProcessEvents on the target hosts for cobalt/sliver/rmm tooling, AADSignInEventsBeta for the cloud trail of the same identity.
let Window = 1h;
let FanOut = DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where LogonType in ("RemoteInteractive","Network","NetworkCleartext","Interactive")
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service","anonymous logon")
| summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceName), Hosts = make_set(DeviceName, 25), Sources = make_set(RemoteIP, 10), Protocols = make_set(LogonType), FirstLogon = min(Timestamp), LastLogon = max(Timestamp) by AccountName, AccountDomain, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| where HostCount >= 3;
FanOut
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
    | summarize BaselineHosts = dcount(DeviceName) by AccountName) on AccountName
| extend BaselineHosts = iff(isempty(BaselineHosts), 0, BaselineHosts)
| where HostCount > BaselineHosts * 2 or BaselineHosts == 0
| project FirstLogon, LastLogon, AccountName, AccountDomain, HostCount, BaselineHosts, Hosts, Sources, Protocols
let Window = 1h;
let FanOut = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventID == 4624
| where LogonType in (3, 10)
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$" and TargetUserName !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE","ANONYMOUS LOGON")
| summarize HostCount = dcount(Computer), Hosts = make_set(Computer, 25), Sources = make_set(IpAddress, 10), Protocols = make_set(LogonType), FirstLogon = min(TimeGenerated), LastLogon = max(TimeGenerated) by TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| where HostCount >= 3;
FanOut
| join kind=leftouter (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where EventID == 4624 and LogonType in (3, 10)
    | summarize BaselineHosts = dcount(Computer) by TargetUserName) on TargetUserName
| extend BaselineHosts = iff(isempty(BaselineHosts), 0, BaselineHosts)
| where HostCount > BaselineHosts * 2 or BaselineHosts == 0
| project FirstLogon, LastLogon, TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, HostCount, BaselineHosts, Hosts, Sources, Protocols
source:windows.security @EventID:4624 @LogonType:(3 OR 10)
#event_simpleName=UserLogon LogonType=/^(3|10)$/ | UserName!=/\$$/ | groupBy([UserName], function=[count(field=aid, distinct=true, as=HostCount), collect([ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4])]) | HostCount>=3
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as first_logon dc(Authentication.dest) as host_count values(Authentication.dest) as hosts values(Authentication.src) as sources from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success Authentication.authentication_method IN ("RemoteInteractive","Network","NetworkCleartext") by Authentication.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where host_count >= 3 AND NOT match(user,"\$$")
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as first_logon dc(Authentication.dest) as host_count values(Authentication.dest) as hosts values(Authentication.src) as sources from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success Authentication.authentication_method IN ("RemoteInteractive","Network","NetworkCleartext") by Authentication.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where host_count >= 3 AND NOT match(user,"\$$")
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net

DeviceEvents

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BleepingComputer
2026-06-15 8 use cases 1 technique 6 kill-chain phases detected

A vulnerability in the SimpleHelp remote management software allows unauthenticated attackers to create privileged technician accounts on servers using the OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication protocol. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Internet-exposed SimpleHelp servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-48558 · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rogue SimpleHelp Technician account created via OIDC bypass (CVE-2026-48558) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — SimpleHelp bug lets hackers create rogue remote support accounts
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] SimpleHelp 'Remote Access.exe' spawning script interpreters on managed endpoints · [LLM] Newly created SimpleHelp Technician immediately exercises privileged actions
Rogue SimpleHelp Technician account created via OIDC bypass (CVE-2026-48558) AIInstallation High
Detects new Technician account registrations/logons in the SimpleHelp server audit log forwarded as syslog. Targets the exact persistence vector from CVE-2026-48558 where forged OIDC identity assertions register an attacker-controlled privileged Technician without MFA. Rationale: Article explicitly names /opt/SimpleHelp/logs/server.log as the audit trail that records 'technician registrations, email addresses, and configuration changes performed by rogue accounts'. Cross-checked with Horizon3.ai disclosure which calls out IoC review focused on 'new authenticated technician users with unknown or suspicious names and/or email addresses' and confirms OIDC is the bypassed code path. Cross-checked against: • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/ • https://www.securityweek.com/vulnerabilities-in-simplehelp-remote-access-software-may-lead-to-system-compromise/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078.004 T1556.006
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate new MSP technician onboarded via OIDC SSO and provisioned just-in-time
  • IT bulk-imports staff into a new SimpleHelp Technician Group on first OIDC rollout
  • Test/QA Technician accounts spun up for SimpleHelp version 5.5.16 upgrade verification
  • Existing technician's UPN changes after a HR rename (creates 'new' OIDC identity)
Suppression filter
| where not (NewUser in ("", "system") or Email endswith "@yourcorp.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full server.log block for the new Technician: capture username, email domain, OIDC subject claim, source IP, Technician Group joined, and whether 'Allow group authenticated logins' is enabled on that group; cross-check the username/email against HR/IdP directory. 2) Contain — if the user is not in the IdP directory or the source IP is foreign, immediately disable the Technician account in SimpleHelp, revoke any active sessions, IP-allowlist Technician logins, and verify the server is on 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 (patch CVE-2026-48558). 3) Hunt — pivot on the same source IP/UA across server.log for prior OIDC probes; review session history for managed-endpoint remote-control or script-execution actions launched by the rogue Technician within the next 24h (feeds UC4).
let LookbackDays = 7d;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ProcessName has "SimpleHelp" or SyslogMessage has "SimpleHelp"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("Technician", "technician")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("created", "registered", "added", "OIDC login", "new technician")
| extend NewUser = extract(@"(?i)technician[^\w]+([\w._-]+@?[\w._-]*)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend Email = extract(@"([\w._%+-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend OidcFlag = iff(SyslogMessage has "OIDC" or SyslogMessage has "openid", "oidc", "other")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, OidcFlag, NewUser, Email, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:simplehelp (@message:*Technician* OR @message:*technician*) (@message:*created* OR @message:*registered* OR @message:*added* OR @message:*"OIDC login"*) (@message:*OIDC* OR @message:*openid*)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Authentication.src) as src values(Authentication.user) as user values(Authentication.signature) as signature from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" (Authentication.signature IN ("TechnicianCreated","TechnicianRegistered","OIDCLogin","technician_added") OR Authentication.action="success") Authentication.authentication_method="OIDC" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where firstSeen >= relative_time(now(),"-7d") | eval suspicious=if(match(user, "(?i)(test|admin[0-9]+|temp|qa|root|svc)") OR len(user)<4 OR match(user,"^[a-z0-9]{8,}$"),1,0)
SimpleHelp 'Remote Access.exe' spawning script interpreters on managed endpoints AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation pivot from CVE-2026-48558: a rogue Technician using SimpleHelp's 'execute scripts' capability against managed endpoints. Looks for the SimpleHelp customer-client binary spawning shells or LOLBin script interpreters, which is the only on-endpoint signal an attacker leaves when abusing the platform. Rationale: Article describes the SimpleHelp Technician role as 'remoting into managed endpoints, executing scripts, and more' — the only on-endpoint footprint of that abuse is the customer-client binary spawning shells. Binary name 'Remote Access.exe' (vendor 'SimpleHelp LTD') corroborated by Arctic Wolf's prior SimpleHelp campaign write-up — kept generic on installation path because SimpleHelp installs vary per deployment. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/arctic-wolf-observes-campaign-exploiting-simplehelp-rmm-software-for-initial-access/ • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/
ATT&CKT1219 T1059 T1072
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Help-desk technician runs a legitimate cmd/PowerShell command during a support call
  • MSP-pushed scheduled scripts (patch installers, log collectors) launched via SimpleHelp remote session
  • SimpleHelp's built-in 'Tools' menu running diagnostic commands (ipconfig, systeminfo)
  • Endpoint inventory script invoked by IT during fleet audit
  • Vendor-supplied update wrapped as a script and pushed through SimpleHelp
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildCmd has_any ("\\Get-ComputerInfo", "\\ipconfig", "systeminfo", "\\WindowsUpdate")) and not (AccountName in~ ("known-helpdesk-svc"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full child command line, SHA256, and the Technician name driving the SimpleHelp session from server.log within ±2 min of the spawn; check if the Technician is a known-good IdP user. 2) Contain — if the Technician is unknown / brand-new / has a suspicious email domain, kill the SimpleHelp session, isolate the affected endpoint via MDE, disable the Technician account on the SimpleHelp server, and rotate any creds typed during the session. 3) Hunt — pivot on the Technician's identity across server.log for every other endpoint they touched in the last 14d; sweep those endpoints for the same parent→child pattern, plus newly written persistence artifacts (services, Run keys, scheduled tasks) attributed to 'Remote Access.exe'.
let Lookback = 7d;
let Lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Remote Access.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("SimpleHelp", "SimpleHelp LTD") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "SimpleHelp"
| where FileName in~ (Lolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 7d;
let Lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\Remote Access.exe" or ActingProcessName =~ "Remote Access.exe"
| where (ActingProcessFileCompany has_any ("SimpleHelp", "SimpleHelp LTD")) or ActingProcessName has "SimpleHelp"
| extend ChildExe = tostring(split(TargetProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where tolower(ChildExe) in (Lolbins)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SimpleHelp Remote Access Spawning Shell or LOLBin Script Interpreter
id: 6a3f1f0a-9b1e-4d2d-8e7f-9c2b8b1f4d22
description: Detects the SimpleHelp customer-client process ('Remote Access.exe', SimpleHelp LTD) spawning shells or LOLBin script interpreters. After CVE-2026-48558, rogue OIDC-registered Technicians can drive arbitrary script execution on managed endpoints via this exact chain.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/simplehelp-bug-lets-hackers-create-rogue-remote-support-accounts/
  - https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/15
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1072
  - attack.execution
  - attack.lateral_movement
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Remote Access.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate help-desk troubleshooting via SimpleHelp remote session
  - MSP-driven scripted maintenance jobs
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\Remote\ Access.exe OR *\\remote\ access.exe OR *\\REMOTE\ ACCESS.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\RegSvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^remote access\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Internet-exposed SimpleHelp servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-48558 AIReconnaissance High
Asset-surface hunt for SimpleHelp servers running 5.5.15 or older / 6.0 pre-release that are reachable from the internet — the entire prerequisite for CVE-2026-48558 exploitation. Lets the SOC drive emergency patching to 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 before opportunistic exploitation. Rationale: Article gives the exact patched versions (5.5.16, 6.0RC2 released June 9 2026) and prerequisite (internet-exposed server with OIDC). Detection joins Defender TVM CveId lookup against DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing so SOC can prioritise the ~14,000-server exposure cited by Horizon3.ai's Shodan analysis. Image [3] in the article also visually confirms a rogue Technician landed on a real server console. Cross-checked against: • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/ • https://cve.threatint.eu/CVE/CVE-2026-48558
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SimpleHelp servers behind reverse-proxy/WAF that Defender marks as IsInternetFacing but are not directly reachable on 443
  • Lab/test SimpleHelp 6.0 pre-release instances that intentionally lag patches
  • DR-replica SimpleHelp servers visible to TVM but powered off / firewall-blocked
  • Servers patched in the last 24h that TVM hasn't yet re-scanned
Suppression filter
| where IsInternetFacing == true
Response runbook
1) Triage — for each hit, confirm the SimpleHelp version via the server's About page or `/configuration/version`, validate OIDC is enabled, and identify which Technician Groups have 'Allow group authenticated logins' set. 2) Contain — if internet-facing and unpatched, immediately apply 5.5.16 (5.x branch) or 6.0RC2, and as a stop-gap put an IP allowlist on Technician logins per SimpleHelp's mitigation guidance; rotate any technician API tokens. 3) Hunt — pull /opt/SimpleHelp/logs/server.log on each exposed host for any Technician created since 2026-06-01 with an unknown email domain, and run UC1 retroactively for the last 30 days.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion,

Newly created SimpleHelp Technician immediately exercises privileged actions AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates a brand-new Technician registration in SimpleHelp server.log with privileged actions (remote-session start, script execution, group/role change) by that same account within minutes. The compressed timeline is the signature of CVE-2026-48558 abuse — legitimate onboarding flows have a HR/training gap. Rationale: Article emphasises that the rogue Technician is *immediately* usable for 'remoting into managed endpoints, executing scripts'. Kill-chain block phase 4 detection hint: 'Newly created Technician accounts immediately exercising privileged actions ... shortly after first login'. The 15-minute window keeps onboarding-with-immediate-use FPs but eliminates legitimate flows where HR creates the account hours before first use. Cross-checked against: • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1098 T1219
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MSP runbook that provisions a Technician and immediately runs a smoke-test remote session
  • Migration scripts during the 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 upgrade that re-create Technicians and validate access
  • Just-in-time access tooling that creates an ephemeral Technician for a single ticket
  • QA engineer creating a Technician and self-testing within minutes
Suppression filter
| where DelaySec >= 5
Response runbook
1) Triage — capture the new Technician's username, email, OIDC sub claim, source IP, and the exact privileged action taken (which managed endpoint did they hit, which script ran). 2) Contain — disable the Technician account in SimpleHelp, kill any in-flight remote sessions to the targeted endpoints, isolate those endpoints via MDE, and snapshot for forensics; if the server is still on a vulnerable version, patch to 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 immediately. 3) Hunt — for the source IP and OIDC sub claim, enumerate all SimpleHelp authentications and every endpoint the rogue Technician interacted with; on each endpoint, run UC2 retro-active and inspect created services, scheduled tasks, and outbound C2 connections from 'Remote Access.exe' or its children.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 15m;
let Creations = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has "SimpleHelp" or SyslogMessage has "SimpleHelp"
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)technician.*?(created|registered|added)"
    | extend NewUser = extract(@"(?i)technician[^\w]+([\w._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(NewUser)
    | project CreateTime = TimeGenerated, NewUser, Computer, CreationMsg = SyslogMessage;
let PrivActions = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has "SimpleHelp" or SyslogMessage has "SimpleHelp"
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("remote session", "script", "group modified", "configuration changed", "role", "privilege")
    | extend ActorUser = extract(@"(?i)(?:user|technician|by)[^\w]+([\w._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(ActorUser)
    | project ActionTime = TimeGenerated, ActorUser, Computer, ActionMsg = SyslogMessage;
Creations
| join kind=inner (PrivActions) on $left.NewUser == $right.ActorUser
| where ActionTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ActionTime, CreateTime)
| project CreateTime, ActionTime, DelaySec, NewUser, Computer, CreationMsg, ActionMsg
| order by ActionTime desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true min(_time) as createTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" Authentication.signature IN ("TechnicianCreated","TechnicianRegistered","technician_added") by Authentication.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| rename user as suspectUser
| join type=inner suspectUser [
    | tstats summariesonly=true min(_time) as actionTime values(Authentication.action) as actions values(Authentication.src) as srcIPs values(Authentication.dest) as targets from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" Authentication.signature IN ("RemoteSessionStarted","ScriptExecuted","TechnicianGroupModified","ConfigChanged","PrivilegeChanged") by Authentication.user
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
    | rename user as suspectUser ]
| eval delaySec=actionTime-createTime
| where delaySec >= 0 AND delaySec <= 900
| convert ctime(createTime) ctime(actionTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as createTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" Authentication.signature IN ("TechnicianCreated","TechnicianRegistered","technician_added") by Authentication.user

    | tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as actionTime values(Authentication.action) as actions values(Authentication.src) as srcIPs values(Authentication.dest) as targets from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" Authentication.signature IN ("RemoteSessionStarted","ScriptExecuted","TechnicianGroupModified","ConfigChanged","PrivilegeChanged") by Authentication.user
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
    | rename user as suspectUser ]
| eval delaySec=actionTime-createTime
| where delaySec >= 0 AND delaySec <= 900
| convert ctime(createTime) ctime(actionTime)

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
