Inbound WebSocket to Vitest Browser API /__vitest_browser_api__ from non-loopback (CVE-2026-53633) AIDelivery High
Hunts external connections to the Vitest Browser Mode WebSocket API exposed by --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0 on default port 63315, targeting the /__vitest_browser_api__ or /__vitest_test__/ paths the CVE-2026-53633 PoC walks through. A remote client hitting these paths while a session is active is the precondition for sendCdpEvent abuse. Rationale: Anchors on the article-named port 63315 and path /__vitest_browser_api__ exposed when --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0 is set. Sentinel ImWebSession URL match catches the exact RPC path; Defender side requires node.exe parent because legitimate inbound to 63315 from a dev laptop should be unprecedented. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer remotely accessing their own watch-mode dev server from a teammate machine on the LAN
  • Internal CI/E2E runner connecting to a dev workstation running Vitest
  • Reverse-proxied Vitest UI behind an internal portal
  • Pen-test or vulnerability scanner probing port 63315
  • Browser-extension developer testing cross-origin to localhost from a different device
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteIP in ("<known-CI-runner-ip>", "<known-developer-laptop-subnet>") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the remote IP and confirm whether the originating host is a known developer/CI source; pull DeviceProcessEvents on the listener host for the Vitest CLI to confirm --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0 and allowWrite/allowExec settings. Step 2 (contain): instruct user to terminate the Vitest watch session immediately, revert vite.config.ts from git, and bind future Vitest sessions to 127.0.0.1 only or remove --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0; isolate workstation if vite.config.ts shows unexpected diff. Step 3 (hunt): search DeviceFileEvents on the same host for vite.config.* writes within the session window, DeviceProcessEvents for browser-spawned node.exe children, and DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound C2 from any node.exe spawned post-config-reload.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where LocalPort == 63315
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted", "ListeningConnectionCreated", "ConnectionAccepted")
| where RemoteIPType !in ("Loopback", "Private") or (RemoteIPType == "Private" and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1", "::1"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest", "@vitest/browser", "vite-plus")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where Url has_any ("/__vitest_browser_api__", "/__vitest_test__/")
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1" and isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| union (
    ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where DstPortNumber == 63315
    | where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1" and isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Inbound Connection to Vitest Browser Mode API Port 63315
id: 9c2f1e4b-7d8a-4f1c-b6e3-2a5d8f1c9e0a
description: Detects inbound network connection to Vitest Browser Mode WebSocket API port 63315 from non-loopback source, the precondition for CVE-2026-53633 CDP-bypass RCE.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Initiated: false
    DestinationPort: 63315
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
  filter_loopback:
    SourceIp:
      - '127.0.0.1'
      - '::1'
  condition: selection and not filter_loopback
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationPort:63315 (@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE)) -@SourceIp:127.0.0.1 -@SourceIp:::1
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=63315 ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| NOT RemoteAddressIP4=/^(127\.|::1$)/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK

vite.config.* overwrite by Chromium/Playwright browser process (CVE-2026-53633) AIInstallation High
Detects browser binaries writing or modifying Vitest/Vite config files in the project root - the exact effect of the CDP Page.setDownloadBehavior + Runtime.evaluate exploit chain. A Chromium-family process should never legitimately write vite.config.ts; this is the highest-fidelity host-side signal for the CVE. Rationale: The article explicitly walks through CDP Page.setDownloadBehavior + Runtime.evaluate using <a download="vite.config.ts"> to overwrite the Vite config. The write is mediated by the browser, so InitiatingProcessFileName == browser binary writing a vite.config.* file is a near-zero-FP signal because browsers never legitimately write project build configs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
ATT&CKT1546 T1574 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually drag-dropping a config file into the browser to view it (extremely rare; usually only reads)
  • Browser-based code editor extension (Stackblitz, Codespaces in-browser) syncing to local disk via File System Access API
  • Playwright codegen tool writing test fixtures with similar filename (would be playwright.config not vite.config)
  • Antivirus/Defender restoring quarantined config file via browser-mediated restore download
  • User intentionally downloading a vite.config.ts sample from a tutorial site into the project root
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): compare the new vite.config.* against the last git commit on disk and the remote main branch - any added imports, child_process/exec/spawn calls, eval, or network fetches indicate compromise. Step 2 (contain): kill the Vitest/Node watch process IMMEDIATELY (reload triggers RCE), revert the file with git checkout, and quarantine any node.exe processes spawned after the file-write timestamp. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the same DeviceId for outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from node.exe in the 10 minutes after the write, DeviceImageLoadEvents showing the browser loading @vitest/@playwright modules, and inbound port 63315 connections in the prior hour to identify the attacker IP.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("vite.config.ts", "vite.config.js", "vite.config.mjs", "vite.config.mts", "vitest.config.ts", "vitest.config.js", "vitest.config.mjs", "vitest.config.mts")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe", "chromium.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "headless_shell.exe", "playwright.exe", "opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("vite.config.ts", "vite.config.js", "vite.config.mjs", "vite.config.mts", "vitest.config.ts", "vitest.config.js", "vitest.config.mjs", "vitest.config.mts")
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe", "chromium.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "headless_shell.exe", "playwright.exe", "opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects Chromium/Playwright/Firefox browser binaries writing vite.config.* or vitest.config.* files - the primary file-system impact of CVE-2026-53633 CDP-bypass RCE.

Vitest Browser Mode CLI bound to 0.0.0.0 with allowWrite/allowExec disabled (CVE-2026-53633 vulnerable config) AIWeaponization Medium
Hunting query for the specific dangerous configuration pattern from the GHSA: --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0 (network-exposed) combined with allowWrite=false/allowExec=false. The article calls out that disabling write/exec gives a false sense of security because CDP RPC is not gated by those flags, so this exact combination is the misconfiguration footprint. Rationale: The article's reproduction explicitly uses `host: '0.0.0.0'` + `allowWrite: false` + `allowExec: false` as the vulnerable config. This combination is the precise misconfiguration that gives a false sense of security per the GHSA narrative - allowWrite/allowExec do not gate CDP, so this CLI/config pattern is the indicator of vulnerable exposure. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
ATT&CKT1190 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal CI test rig that legitimately needs network-exposed Vitest for cross-device E2E testing
  • Developer pairing on a remote dev VM where host=0.0.0.0 is required for VPN access
  • Demo/training environment where host=0.0.0.0 is set deliberately for a workshop
  • Container-based dev environment (Devcontainer/Docker) where 0.0.0.0 is needed to reach the container port
  • Vitest UI dashboard intentionally shared on the LAN for stakeholder review
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("<ci-runner-host-pattern>", "<sanctioned-test-rig>") and InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): confirm whether this is a known/sanctioned CI runner or developer workflow; correlate with DeviceNetworkEvents for any external IPs that have hit port 63315 since the Vitest process started. Step 2 (contain): instruct the user to either upgrade @vitest/browser to a patched version (>5.0.0-beta.3 / >4.1.7 / >3.2.4) or bind to 127.0.0.1; if external connections were observed, kill the process and inspect vite.config.* and project tree for tampering. Step 3 (hunt): pivot to all hosts running @vitest/browser in vulnerable ranges via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory and SBOM data; check DeviceFileEvents on each for browser-mediated config-file writes in the prior 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest", "@vitest/browser", "vite-plus")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--browser.api.host=0.0.0.0", "--browser.api.host 0.0.0.0")
| extend WriteDisabled = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("allowWrite=false", "allowWrite: false")
| extend ExecDisabled = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("allowExec=false", "allowExec: false")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, WriteDisabled, ExecDisabled
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "node") or TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "node")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest", "@vitest/browser", "vite-plus") or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest", "@vitest/browser", "vite-plus")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--browser.api.host=0.0.0.0", "--browser.api.host 0.0.0.0") or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--browser.api.host=0.0.0.0", "--browser.api.host 0.0.0.0")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Vitest Browser Mode Bound to All Interfaces (CVE-2026-53633 Risk Pattern)
id: 1b7e9f2d-5a3c-4d6e-8f1a-2c9b7e5d3f1a
description: Detects Node.js process launching Vitest with --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0, exposing the Browser Mode WebSocket API to the network and enabling CVE-2026-53633 CDP-bypass RCE.
references:

level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE)) @CommandLine:(*vitest* AND *--browser.api.host=0.0.0.0*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)vitest", field=CommandLine)
| regex("--browser\\.api\\.host=0\\.0\\.0\\.0", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="node.exe" OR Processes.process_name="node") AND Processes.process="*vitest*" AND Processes.process="*--browser.api.host=0.0.0.0*" by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)allowWrite=false|allowExec=false") OR match(process, "(?i)--browser.api.host=0\.0\.0\.0")
vite.config.* modification followed by rapid node.exe re-execution within 10s (CVE-2026-53633 RCE trigger) AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates a vite.config.* / vitest.config.* file modification with a node.exe process creation on the same host within 10 seconds - the event-triggered execution chain the GHSA describes where Vitest reloads the changed config and runs attacker-controlled Node.js code. The narrow temporal window distinguishes this from manual edit-and-rerun developer workflows. Rationale: The article's RCE step is explicit: 'Vitest reloads the changed config' after the overwrite, executing attacker-controlled Node.js. The 10-second window catches the auto-reload (which is sub-second in practice) while excluding the normal developer save-and-rerun pattern (humans take longer to retrigger). Joining on DeviceId/DvcHostname/aid ties the file-write to the very next node spawn on the same host. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using a hot-reload watcher (vitest --watch) that re-runs within seconds of manual edit
  • IDE auto-save plugin saving vite.config.ts and the test runner picking it up immediately
  • Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook that rewrites vite.config.ts then re-runs vitest
  • npm/pnpm install or upgrade rewriting config and triggering postinstall test run
  • CI build pipeline that templates vite.config.ts then immediately invokes vitest
Suppression filter
| where WriterProcess !in~ ("node.exe", "git.exe", "husky.exe", "code.exe", "devenv.exe") and not (ProcParent =~ "husky.exe" or ProcParent =~ "git.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): inspect the new vite.config.* diff vs git HEAD - any added child_process.exec/spawn, eval, dynamic import of remote URL, or fetch() calls indicates exploitation. Step 2 (contain): kill all node.exe descendants spawned after the file-write timestamp on this host; isolate workstation if config shows attacker payload; revert vite.config.* via git. Step 3 (hunt): pull DeviceNetworkEvents for the node.exe PID for outbound C2; check DeviceNetworkEvents on port 63315 inbound in the prior 30 minutes to identify the attacker source IP; sweep other dev workstations for the same Vitest version + 0.0.0.0 binding pattern.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 10;
let ConfigWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("vite.config.ts", "vite.config.js", "vite.config.mjs", "vite.config.mts", "vitest.config.ts", "vitest.config.js", "vitest.config.mjs")
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
    | project FileTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ConfigPath = FolderPath, ConfigFile = FileName, WriterProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let NodeSpawns = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "node")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest", "vite")
    | project ProcTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ProcParent = InitiatingProcessFileName, AccountName;
ConfigWrites
| join kind=inner NodeSpawns on DeviceId
| where ProcTime between (FileTime .. FileTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, FileTime)
| project FileTime, ProcTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, ConfigFile, ConfigPath, WriterProcess, WriterCmd, ProcParent, ProcCmd
| order by FileTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 10;
let ConfigWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("vite.config.ts", "vite.config.js", "vite.config.mjs", "vite.config.mts", "vitest.config.ts", "vitest.config.js", "vitest.config.mjs")
    | where EventType in~ ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
    | project FileTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ConfigFile = TargetFileName, ConfigPath = TargetFilePath, WriterProcess = ActingProcessName;
let NodeSpawns = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "node")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest", "vite")
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ProcCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, ProcParent = ActingProcessName, ActorUsername;
ConfigWrites
| join kind=inner NodeSpawns on DvcHostname
| where ProcTime between (FileTime .. FileTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, FileTime)
| project FileTime, ProcTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigFile, ConfigPath, WriterProcess, ProcParent, ProcCmd
| order by FileTime desc
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|mts)$/i
| FileTime := _time
| ConfigFile := TargetFileName
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i | regex("(?i)vitest|vite", field=CommandLine) | ProcTime := _time | ProcCmd := CommandLine}, field=aid, include=[ProcTime, ProcCmd])
| DelaySec := ProcTime - FileTime
| DelaySec >= 0 AND DelaySec <= 10
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ConfigFile, ProcCmd, DelaySec], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as fileTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name IN ("vite.config.ts","vite.config.js","vite.config.mjs","vite.config.mts","vitest.config.ts","vitest.config.js") AND Filesystem.action IN ("modified","created","written") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host | join type=inner host [ | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as procTime values(Processes.process) as procCmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" AND Processes.process="*vitest*" by Processes.dest, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename dest as host ] | where procTime >= fileTime AND (procTime - fileTime) <= 10 | eval delaySec = procTime - fileTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as fileTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name IN ("vite.config.ts","vite.config.js","vite.config.mjs","vite.config.mts","vitest.config.ts","vitest.config.js") AND Filesystem.action IN ("modified","created","written") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host | join type=inner host [ | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as procTime values(Processes.process) as procCmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" AND Processes.process="*vitest*" by Processes.dest, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename dest as host ] | where procTime >= fileTime AND (procTime - fileTime) <= 10 | eval delaySec = procTime - fileTime
Chromium/Playwright browser spawning node.exe or shell interpreter (CVE-2026-53633 post-RCE) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects a browser process spawning Node, PowerShell, cmd, or scripting hosts as a child - the visible aftermath of CDP Runtime.evaluate executing attacker JavaScript that escapes the browser context via the compromised Vitest bridge. In Playwright/Vitest setups, the browser should never legitimately spawn these interpreters. Rationale: The article shows CDP Runtime.evaluate executes attacker JS inside the browser, and the config-overwrite path triggers Node code execution. While Node typically spawns OUTSIDE the browser tree, the immediate post-exploit hands-on-keyboard often involves the browser PID parenting follow-on payloads (especially in Playwright/headless_shell setups where browser and runner share parents). Browser->shell/Node is anomalous in any normal user session. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Electron apps embedding Chromium that fork node helpers (Slack, VSCode, Discord, Teams) - parent image looks like a browser binary
  • Chrome extensions using Native Messaging Host invoking node.exe as the host
  • Browser-launched IDE protocol handlers (vscode://, jetbrains://) spawning a shell to open a project
  • WebDriver/Selenium auto-launching node test runners from browser sessions
  • Playwright codegen feature spawning a node REPL for test recording
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("electron.exe", "slack.exe", "code.exe", "teams.exe", "discord.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\AppData\\Local\\slack\\", "\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the child process command line - empty/unusual node args (-e, --eval, base64, network fetch) is high-confidence malicious; check if the parent browser PID was a Playwright session managed by Vitest. Step 2 (contain): kill the child interpreter tree and the parent browser; isolate workstation if the command line shows network egress or persistence writes; force-rotate any developer secrets present in env vars. Step 3 (hunt): correlate the child PID with DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound C2, DeviceFileEvents for dropper artefacts, and DeviceRegistryEvents for autorun additions; pivot to inbound port 63315 connections in the prior hour to identify the attacker IP.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe", "chromium.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "headless_shell.exe", "playwright.exe", "opera.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "python.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe", "chromium.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "headless_shell.exe", "playwright.exe", "opera.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "node", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "python.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Chromium/Playwright browser loading @vitest or @playwright Node modules (CVE-2026-53633 RPC bridge) AIInstallation Medium
Detects browser processes loading DLLs/modules from node_modules/@vitest or node_modules/@playwright paths - the in-process signature of the Vitest Browser Mode WebSocket RPC bridge being active and reachable. Combined with inbound port 63315 traffic, this localises which workstations are exposing the vulnerable bridge. Rationale: The article identifies @vitest/browser, @playwright/browser, and vite-plus as the affected packages providing the CDP-capable bridge. Browser processes loading these node_modules paths is the in-process indicator the bridge is hosted - distinct from a normal user browsing the web, where node_modules are never image-loaded into the browser. Sentinel left empty: ASIM has no clean image-load equivalent and SecurityEvent doesn't carry per-DLL load events without Sysmon forwarding. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
ATT&CKT1574 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Other Playwright-based test frameworks (Cypress, Webdriver.io) loading the same @playwright modules on dev machines
  • Electron-bundled apps that ship @playwright for in-app browser automation
  • Developer workstations running Playwright codegen or trace viewer separately from Vitest
  • CI runner image that pre-warms @playwright into a browser cache
  • Storybook or other dev-tool that embeds @vitest/browser for component testing
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("<ci-runner-host-pattern>") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\AppData\\Local\\ms-playwright\\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId in the same window - if port 63315 inbound from non-loopback is also present, this is the vulnerable config in use. Step 2 (contain): if external inbound 63315 traffic correlates, instruct user to upgrade @vitest/browser past the affected ranges (>5.0.0-beta.3 / >4.1.7 / >3.2.4) or revert to 127.0.0.1 binding; check vite.config.* for tampering. Step 3 (hunt): build an organisation-wide inventory of Vitest Browser Mode usage via this query, cross-reference with the affected version ranges in DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory, and prioritise patching for any host that also shows 0.0.0.0 binding.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe", "chromium.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "headless_shell.exe", "playwright.exe", "opera.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any ("node_modules\\@vitest\\", "node_modules/@vitest/", "node_modules\\@playwright\\", "node_modules/@playwright/", "node_modules\\vite-plus\\", "node_modules/vite-plus/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| summarize Loads = count(), Samples = make_set(FolderPath, 5), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by LastSeen desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails

The Hacker News
2026-06-15 11 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email. The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] INFINITERED REDCap backdoor SHA256 sighting (UNC6508) · [LLM] Workspace admin / service account creating forwarding rules across many mailboxes · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Network callback to UNC6508 C2 IP 23.169.65.49 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Google Workspace content-compliance rule BCC'ing mail to external address · [LLM] Bulk mailbox export or Takeout shortly after Workspace rule creation · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
INFINITERED REDCap backdoor SHA256 sighting (UNC6508) AIInstallation Medium
Sight any of the seven GTIG-published INFINITERED hashes on Windows/Linux endpoints or via file-event telemetry. INFINITERED trojanizes REDCap system files for credential harvesting and HTTP-cookie C2; any sighting is a direct UNC6508 incident. Rationale: All seven SHA256 hashes are explicit, published GTIG IOCs for INFINITERED. Hash matches are zero-FP and the article's central malware family. Cross-checked against MITRE ATT&CK T1554 (Compromise Host Software Binary) for the upgrade-process hijack behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR/threat-intel teams running hash sweeps from EDR consoles
  • Malware sandbox uploads of the same sample from analyst workstations
  • VirusTotal CLI tooling on dedicated reverse-engineering hosts
  • Security-tooling self-test using known-bad hash corpora
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","vt.exe","sandboxiedcomlaunch.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the device runs REDCap (verify host role / hostname pattern / installed apps); pull the full file-event tree around the hash sighting and check whether INFINITERED dropped during a REDCap upgrade. Contain: isolate the host via Defender/Falcon network-isolation, snapshot the REDCap install directory before remediation, revoke credentials of any REDCap service account that authenticated from that host since Sep 2023. Hunt: search for outbound HTTP traffic with anomalous Cookie headers from the same host (INFINITERED takes commands via cookies), pivot on the C2 IP 23.169.65.49, and audit Google Workspace admin actions performed by any account credentialled on this host.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7","db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136","c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b","8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec","51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045","4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b","58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Network callback to UNC6508 C2 IP 23.169.65.49 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunt any inbound or outbound network session involving 23.169.65.49 — the GTIG-published UNC6508 C2 IP. Because INFINITERED uses HTTP cookies over standard ports, look at process+IP, not port. Rationale: 23.169.65.49 is the GTIG-published UNC6508 C2 IP. Single-IP hunt across 30 days catches dormant comms; pairing with InitiatingProcessFileName surfaces which binary on the REDCap server is calling out. CloudWatch left empty because the IP detection telemetry naturally lives in EDR / NSM, not CloudTrail — VPC Flow could carry it but is out of scope for the article's REDCap-server target. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platforms (MISP, OpenCTI) actively pulling IOC pages that embed the IP
  • Analyst manually curling/pinging the IP during triage
  • Sandboxes detonating the INFINITERED sample with live network
  • TOR-exit or shared-hosting collisions if the IP gets reassigned
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("misp.exe","opencti-worker.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe") or InitiatingProcessAccountName !has "threat-intel"
Response runbook
Triage: identify host(s) calling 23.169.65.49, the initiating process, and the user context; confirm whether host runs REDCap. Contain: block 23.169.65.49 at egress proxy and firewall, isolate any REDCap server seen calling out, take memory snapshot before reimaging. Hunt: review HTTP request Cookie headers from that host (INFINITERED carries C2 in cookies), search REDCap log files for unusual page-load patterns from anomalous source IPs, and check for lateral logons originating from the same source-account in the previous 30 days.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "23.169.65.49" or LocalIP == "23.169.65.49"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP, LocalPort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr == "23.169.65.49" or SrcIpAddr == "23.169.65.49" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationIP == "23.169.65.49" or SourceIP == "23.169.65.49" | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, SourceUserName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Google Workspace content-compliance rule BCC'ing mail to external address AIActions on Objectives High
Detect creation or modification of a Google Workspace domain content compliance rule that BCCs/copies matched mail to an address outside the organisation — the exact exfil mechanism UNC6508 used (rule named "Patroit", ~150 keywords incl. "chikungunya"). This is a Workspace admin action, not endpoint telemetry. Rationale: The article explicitly names the misspelled rule ("Patroit") and the standout keyword ("chikungunya"). Detection logic anchors on the GWS admin action that creates/changes a CONTENT_COMPLIANCE rule with a BCC/external-add-header action — the exact exfil primitive. Sentinel/Defender/Falcon left empty because this telemetry lives in Google Workspace Admin Reports API, not Microsoft/CrowdStrike products. Cross-checked MITRE T1114.003 (Email Forwarding Rule) — GTIG flags the use of *domain-level* content compliance for this as new behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/ • https://support.google.com/a/answer/1346934
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1564.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate DLP rule onboarding that copies sensitive mail to a security mailbox
  • Compliance / e-discovery archiving rules pointing at a vendor inbox
  • Newly onboarded mail-archive vendors (Mimecast, Proofpoint Archive) requiring a journal/BCC address
  • Internal IT testing of mail-routing changes against personal Gmail accounts
Suppression filter
NOT (@actor.email:(security-* OR compliance-* OR archive-svc*) AND @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:(*mimecast.com* OR *proofpoint.com* OR *barracuda.com* OR *journal@*))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full NEW_VALUE / rule definition from the audit event, identify the BCC address and rule keywords, confirm the actor's account and source IP. Contain: disable the rule via Admin Console, suspend the actor's admin session, force re-auth with phishing-resistant MFA, rotate admin credentials. Hunt: list every domain content compliance rule with an outbound BCC/header-add action across all OUs, check Reports API for all rule changes back to Sept 2023, audit which mailboxes the rule scoped over and treat any matched mail since rule-creation as compromised; review admin role grants in the same window.
title: Google Workspace Content Compliance Rule with External BCC (UNC6508)
id: d27b8a91-3f4e-4c6b-8a09-7e5b0f3a2d44
description: Detects creation or change of a Google Workspace domain content compliance / routing rule that copies or BCCs matched mail to an external address, mirroring UNC6508's "Patroit" rule.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/chinese-hackers-abused-google-workspace.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1114.003
  - attack.t1564.008
logsource:
  product: google_workspace
  service: admin
detection:
  selection:
    eventName:
      - 'CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING'
      - 'CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING'
      - 'CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING'
      - 'CHANGE_APPLICATION_SETTING'
    parameters.SETTING_NAME:
      - 'CONTENT_COMPLIANCE'
      - 'OBJECTIONABLE_CONTENT'
      - 'ROUTING'
  keywords:
    parameters.NEW_VALUE|contains:
      - 'Bcc'
      - 'addHeader'
      - 'Patroit'
      - 'chikungunya'
  condition: selection and keywords
level: high
source:google.workspace @event.type:APPLICATION_SETTINGS @event.name:(CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING OR CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING OR CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING OR CHANGE_APPLICATION_SETTING) (@event.parameters.SETTING_NAME:(CONTENT_COMPLIANCE OR OBJECTIONABLE_CONTENT OR ROUTING)) (@event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*Bcc* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*Patroit* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*chikungunya*)
APPLICATION
index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:admin" (event.name="CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING" OR event.name="CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING" OR event.name="CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING" OR event.name="CHANGE_APPLICATION_SETTING") (event.parameters.SETTING_NAME="CONTENT_COMPLIANCE" OR event.parameters.SETTING_NAME="OBJECTIONABLE_CONTENT" OR event.parameters.SETTING_NAME="ROUTING") 
| rex field=event.parameters.NEW_VALUE "(?i)(?<bcc_addr>[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@(?!yourcorp\.com|your-other-domain\.com)[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" 
| search bcc_addr=* OR event.parameters.NEW_VALUE="*Patroit*" OR event.parameters.NEW_VALUE="*chikungunya*" 
| table _time actor.email actor.callerType event.name event.parameters.SETTING_NAME event.parameters.NEW_VALUE bcc_addr ipAddress
Bulk mailbox export or Takeout shortly after Workspace rule creation AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlate a content-compliance / forwarding rule creation event with a Google Takeout, mailbox-export, or large data-export job initiated within 7 days. Mirrors UNC6508's pattern of standing up exfil rules to drain research/defence mail. Rationale: Article describes high-volume theft of research/defence email — operators typically pair forwarding rules with bulk export jobs. SPL joins admin-rule-create events to subsequent data-export events by the same actor within 7 days, matching the article's collection pattern. Other platforms left empty: telemetry is Google Workspace-only. Sigma left empty because this is a multi-event temporal correlation, which Sigma cannot express cleanly per the rule (counts / time-window join). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/002/ • https://support.google.com/a/answer/100458
ATT&CKT1114.002 T1020 T1567.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Departing employee performing a legitimate Takeout under HR-approved policy
  • Mailbox migration projects to a new tenant
  • Legal/eDiscovery exports during litigation hold
  • IT bulk-archive jobs scheduled after policy review
Suppression filter
NOT (@actor.email:(it-admin* OR ediscovery* OR legalhold*) AND @event.parameters.REASON:(*offboarding* OR *legal-hold* OR *migration*))
Response runbook
Triage: review which mailboxes the rule scoped over, what data the export contained, and whether the destination Drive/Takeout download IP matches the actor's normal pattern. Contain: revoke the export download URL, disable the actor's account, recall any active OAuth tokens, kill in-flight Takeout jobs. Hunt: enumerate all data-export events since the rule was created, list every mailbox whose mail matched the rule's keywords during its active window, search for OAuth grants to non-corporate apps in the same period, and assess whether attacker accessed Drive content tagged with the rule's keywords (chikungunya, defense, research).
source:google.workspace @event.name:(TAKEOUT_CREATED OR DATA_EXPORT OR CREATE_DATA_TRANSFER_REQUEST OR USER_DATA_EXPORT OR DOWNLOAD) @event.parameters.APPLICATION_NAME:(Gmail OR Mail OR Drive)
APPLICATION
index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:admin" event.name IN ("CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING","CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING") event.parameters.SETTING_NAME IN ("CONTENT_COMPLIANCE","ROUTING","DEFAULT_ROUTING") earliest=-14d 
| eval rule_actor=actor.email, rule_time=_time 
| join type=inner rule_actor [ search index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:*" event.name IN ("DOWNLOAD","DATA_EXPORT","TAKEOUT_CREATED","CREATE_DATA_TRANSFER_REQUEST","USER_DATA_EXPORT") earliest=-14d | eval rule_actor=actor.email, export_time=_time | table rule_actor export_time event.name event.parameters.* ipAddress ] 
| where export_time > rule_time AND export_time < rule_time + 604800 
| table rule_time export_time rule_actor event.name event.parameters.SETTING_NAME ipAddress
Workspace admin / service account creating forwarding rules across many mailboxes AIInstallation Medium
Detect a single admin or service account creating or modifying mail forwarding, BCC, or delegation settings against many distinct user mailboxes in a short window — UNC6508 ultimately needed domain-admin rights to install the org-wide content-compliance rule and similar fan-out is the wider exfil pattern. Rationale: Article: UNC6508 walked from initial REDCap foothold → domain-admin → cross-tenant rule install. A single admin/service account flipping mail-forwarding on 10+ mailboxes in an hour is the fan-out shape this campaign produced; threshold derived from typical per-day admin churn (sub-10 in most tenants). Sigma omitted because the detection is a count/threshold over a time bucket, which the rule says to skip. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/
ATT&CKT1098.002 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Change.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT bulk-onboarding script provisioning vacation auto-responders for new hires
  • Mail-migration tooling re-applying forwarding settings during cutover
  • M&A activity bulk-mapping mailboxes to a new domain
  • Helpdesk macro that re-enables forwarding for a department after a policy change
Suppression filter
NOT (@actor.email:(provisioning-svc* OR migration-svc* OR hr-onboarding*) AND @event.parameters.REASON:(*onboarding* OR *migration*))
Response runbook
Triage: identify the actor account, source IP, and the target mailbox list; confirm whether the actor is a real admin or a service account with stolen tokens. Contain: suspend the actor account, revoke OAuth refresh tokens, force re-auth on all admin roles with phishing-resistant MFA, roll back forwarding/delegation changes on the targeted mailboxes. Hunt: pull all admin actions by the actor for the prior 30 days, look for the actor logging in from anomalous geo/ASN, check whether the same IP touched the published UNC6508 C2 (23.169.65.49), and audit role-grant changes that gave the actor admin rights in the first place.
source:google.workspace @event.name:(CHANGE_USER_SETTING OR CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING OR CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING) @event.parameters.SETTING_NAME:(EMAIL_FORWARDING OR FORWARDING OR VACATION_RESPONDER OR DELEGATED_ACCESS OR MAIL_DELEGATION)
APPLICATION
index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:admin" (event.name IN ("CHANGE_USER_SETTING","CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING") (event.parameters.SETTING_NAME IN ("EMAIL_FORWARDING","FORWARDING","VACATION_RESPONDER","DELEGATED_ACCESS","MAIL_DELEGATION") OR event.parameters.NEW_VALUE="*forward*")) earliest=-1d 
| bin _time span=1h 
| stats dcount(event.parameters.USER_EMAIL) as TargetedUsers values(event.parameters.SETTING_NAME) as Settings values(ipAddress) as srcIPs by _time actor.email 
| where TargetedUsers >= 10 
| sort - _time
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents

        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code .vscode/tasks.json or launch.json written by git clone or shell AIDelivery Medium
Detects creation of .vscode/tasks.json, launch.json or settings.json files dropped by git/curl/wget/shells. UNK_DeadDrop, TaskJacker and the December 2025 Contagious Interview pivot all weaponize the VS Code 'runOn: folderOpen' task definition so opening the cloned folder fires the payload with zero further interaction. Rationale: Article explicitly names runOn:folderOpen on .vscode/tasks.json (and the TaskJacker variant dropping tasks.json into existing repos). Pivoting on the file path + non-IDE writer surfaces the dropper before VS Code is even launched.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1195.001 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running 'yo code' or a VS Code extension scaffolder
  • CI bootstrap script writing tasks.json into a fresh checkout
  • Bash-based Dockerfile scaffolder syncing IDE config
  • User pulling dotfiles repo via 'git clone' that legitimately includes .vscode/
  • Cookiecutter / cargo-generate templating tasks.json
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("yo.exe","cookiecutter.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "clone --template"
Response runbook
Triage: read the new tasks.json content — look for 'runOn':'folderOpen' and any shell, runtime or URL in the 'command' field; check git reflog for the originating clone URL and compare against the user's normal repo prefixes. Contain: kill any Code.exe/Cursor.exe process whose --folder-uri points at this repo, quarantine the tasks.json, and isolate the host if a payload already fired. Hunt: pivot on DeviceNetworkEvents from the same DeviceId for outbound traffic to 23.137.105.75 and the UNK_DeadDrop domain list; sweep all hosts that cloned the same remote URL.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @"\.vscode\"
| where FileName in~ ("tasks.json","launch.json","settings.json")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","wsl.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","explorer.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\" or TargetFilePath has "/.vscode/"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("tasks.json","launch.json","settings.json")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("git.exe","git","wsl.exe","bash.exe","sh","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","explorer.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code or Cursor spawning shell or script interpreter (folderOpen auto-execution) AIInstallation High
Detects Code.exe / Cursor.exe spawning cmd, PowerShell, wscript, cscript, node, python or bash with download/exec semantics in the command line. UNK_DeadDrop, TaskJacker and the December 2025 Contagious Interview pivot all weaponize VS Code's runOn:folderOpen so the IDE itself becomes the parent of the loader. Rationale: Article: 'a shell script for macOS and Linux and a VBScript for Windows … installs a malicious VS Code extension (VSIX)' fired by runOn:folderOpen. Parent=Code/Cursor with child interpreter + download/extension-install verbs is the article's exact execution shape.
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Devcontainer post-create scripts pulling dependencies
  • Cursor.exe shelling out to node/python for the in-IDE assistant
  • VS Code remote-SSH bootstrap downloading vscode-server
  • 'code --install-extension' from an admin pushing org-mandated extensions
  • Tutorial 'first run' commands the user pastes into the IDE terminal
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "vscode-server"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "--install-extension ms-vscode"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "--install-extension ms-python"
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine plus tasks.json content (UC 1) for the same DeviceId — confirm the cmd line maps to a 'command'/'args' field in tasks.json. Contain: kill Code.exe/Cursor.exe for the user, suspend the user's session if a payload completed, and quarantine the downloaded artifact at the path in the command line. Hunt: pivot on the downloaded file's SHA256 across the fleet; correlate to UC 5 (23.137.105.75:5173) and UC 7 (UNK_DeadDrop domains) on the same DeviceId within 5 minutes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","DownloadFile","FromBase64String","--install-extension","bitsadmin","certutil","iwr ","Net.WebClient","vsix","chmod +x")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\Code - Insiders.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\Cursor.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\mshta.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\python.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\bash.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\wsl.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","DownloadFile","FromBase64String","--install-extension","bitsadmin","certutil","Net.WebClient","vsix","chmod +x")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Code.exe or Cursor.exe --install-extension invoked by non-interactive parent AIInstallation High
Detects code.exe / cursor.exe --install-extension being driven by cmd.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe or PowerShell. The Windows UNK_DeadDrop pipeline runs a VBScript loader that shells out to CMD which calls code.exe --install-extension to install the Google-themed VSIX without UI; Yeeth Security's ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev extensions land the same way. Rationale: Article: 'the VBScript payload to run a CMD file, which then installs the extension'. Parent in (cmd/wscript/etc.) + Code/Cursor --install-extension is a near-zero-noise pivot — humans install via UI; only automation drives this CLI form.
ATT&CKT1176 T1059.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SCCM/Intune extension push from cmd-wrapped scriptlet
  • Devcontainer postCreateCommand installing extensions via shell
  • DevEx onboarding script seeding new joiners with extensions
  • Chocolatey/winget VS Code extension package install
  • Engineer scripting an extension reinstall in a dotfiles repo
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "intune"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "sccm"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "ms-vscode."
Response runbook
Triage: capture the VSIX path/identifier from the --install-extension argument; check the writer of the .vsix file via DeviceFileEvents and the publisher metadata in %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\<id>\package.json — flag publishers ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev or any 'Google service' impersonation. Contain: uninstall the extension (code --uninstall-extension <id>), delete the extension folder, kill Code/Cursor for the user. Hunt: across the fleet for the same extension id and SHA256 of the VSIX; pivot to UC 4 for outbound to graph.microsoft.com / sharepoint.com from the same DeviceId.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","code-tunnel.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--install-extension"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wmic.exe","mshta.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\Cursor.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\code-tunnel.exe"
| where CommandLine has "--install-extension"
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\mshta.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\wmic.exe"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code (Code.exe) outbound Microsoft Graph / SharePoint traffic from non-IDE child AICommand & Control High
Detects Code.exe / Cursor.exe spawning a shell or interpreter that hits graph.microsoft.com or *.sharepoint.com. Yeeth Security's ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev, ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools and OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools VSIXes use a SharePoint site as command queue and Microsoft Graph as the data channel — abusing trusted Microsoft endpoints to look like normal IDE telemetry. Rationale: Article (Yeeth Security): 'A JavaScript layer that handles all C2 communication via Microsoft Graph API and SharePoint' and 'A SharePoint site functioning as a command queue, victim registry, and exfiltration channel.' Detecting Code/Cursor parenting an interpreter hitting those endpoints catches the C2 channel without relying on a known C2 IP.
ATT&CKT1102 T1071.001 T1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VS Code GitHub Copilot Chat shelling out to node for Graph/SharePoint MCP server
  • ms-vscode.sharepoint or PnP PowerShell extension legitimately calling Graph
  • User pasting a 'Invoke-RestMethod graph.microsoft.com' tutorial into the integrated terminal
  • Devops engineer running az / pnp / Graph cmdlets in the IDE terminal
  • Settings Sync conflict resolution scripts
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "PnP.PowerShell"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "Microsoft.Graph"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "copilot-chat"
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full CommandLine and 30 min of process tree for the DeviceId; verify the VSIX list under %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions for ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev*, ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools*, OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools*. Contain: uninstall the extension(s), kill Code/Cursor for the user, revoke any OAuth tokens the user has issued to 'Microsoft Graph PowerShell' or unfamiliar app IDs in the last 7 days. Hunt: query CloudAppEvents / AADSignInEventsBeta for the user's Graph activity, look for unusual ObjectId/RawEventData paths against a SharePoint site the user doesn't normally touch; pivot UC 3 for the original VSIX install.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","bash.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("graph.microsoft.com","sharepoint.com","/v1.0/me/drive","/_api/web","Invoke-RestMethod","Invoke-WebRequest","Net.WebClient")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\Code - Insiders.exe"
    or ParentProcessName endswith @"\Cursor.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\python.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\bash.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("graph.microsoft.com","sharepoint.com","/v1.0/me/drive","/_api/web","Invoke-RestMethod","Invoke-WebRequest","Net.WebClient")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound TCP to UNK_DeadDrop C2 23.137.105[.]75:5173 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects any process connecting to 23.137.105.75 on TCP 5173. Proofpoint named this exact IP:port as the UNK_DeadDrop HTTP POST sink for wallet/credential ZIPs harvested from Linux, macOS and Windows victims. Rationale: Article: 'exfiltrate the results to the server ("23.137.105[.]75:5173") via an HTTP POST request.' One published IP + uncommon high port (5173 is Vite's default but unusual for outbound) = near-zero FP IOC alert.
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer reaching a third-party Vite dev server happens to share the IP (extremely unlikely — public IP, not localhost)
  • Penetration test using the same IP as a callback
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonation in the same environment
  • Security researcher manually triaging the IOC from a sandbox VM
  • Reuse of the IP by another tenant after takedown
Response runbook
Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName on the DeviceId — confirm it's a shell, node, python, Code/Cursor child or a freshly-dropped binary; pull the user's Downloads / cloned-repo paths from DeviceFileEvents around the connection time. Contain: block 23.137.105.75 at egress/EDR network containment, isolate the DeviceId, force credential rotation for any browser-saved or wallet-extension secrets on that host. Hunt: query the last 30 days for any host that ever hit this IP, the article's domain list, or downloaded a VSIX matching the Yeeth Security names; rotate cloud / git credentials for affected users.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "23.137.105.75"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "23.137.105.75"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc
